data.title: Klapy (Udiča) – a drawing of the hillfort in the Púchov culture period
data.excerpt: Hillforts in the mountains of northern Slovakia follow a recurring pattern: a larger hill with fairly steep slopes, a slight rampart and, behind it, a dense network of small settlement terraces. Our member Nika (Art by Vesna) has drawn Klapy above Udiča as it may once have looked, using aerial photographs and a lidar model of the site.

children.text: We have already written in the past about

, which lies in the cadastral area of the village of Udiča. We have likewise written about several other hillforts that have a very similar manner of construction and arrangement of houses. These are occupations of larger hills with fairly steep slopes, on which there is a slight rampart and behind it a fairly dense network of small settlement terraces, on which the houses and farm buildings of the inhabitants were probably situated. From our experience of the excavations we have taken part in recently, it is quite clear that this way of building fortifications and hilltop settlements began to be used in the mountain regions of Slovakia by the people of the Lusatian culture at some point around the transition from the Final Bronze Age to the Hallstatt period. Most of them were then occupied in later periods by the people of the Púchov culture as well (the La Tène and Roman periods); some of them were occupied in this later period only to a lesser extent and by less wealthy inhabitants, but some, including Klapy, were very wealthy in the Púchov culture period too, as is shown by the luxury objects that were found there.

We often find this type of occupation in the mountain regions of northern Slovakia. So far, however, there is only a minimum of depictions of what such a hillfort might have looked like in antiquity. Most ordinary people interested in history therefore find it hard to imagine what such a hillfort may originally have looked like. We are therefore very glad that our member

), who draws very beautifully, undertook to try to draw such a hillfort – specifically Klapy – in such a way that it would come as close as possible to our idea of its original appearance. As a basis we used, besides the aerial photographs we had taken in the past, our own insights from the site, but above all we were greatly helped by the lidar
model of the hillfort provided to us by Ing. Tibor Lieskovský

. The picture captures both the course of the presumed fortification and the possible appearance of the buildings on the individual terraces. In the foreground there are kilns for firing pottery; here we drew on the find of such kilns in nearby Nosice. Below the hillfort there were settlements of the Púchov culture period, where it can reasonably be assumed that such production areas with kilns and other installations were also located.
